_doc: Acknowledged reds — vibe-ic#1025. Adjudicated by
vibe-ic-marketplace/plugins/vibe-ic/programs/gate_red_since_check.py.
A row here grants NO leniency. The hygiene suite still exits 1 for every
FAIL exactly as it did before this file existed, so there is nothing a row
can silence and no green a row can buy. The ONLY thing a row does is start
a clock that gate_red_since_check will fail on once `max_commits` is
exceeded. Adding a row is therefore taking on a deadline, never escaping
one.
Delete the row in the SAME commit that fixes the gate. A row that outlives
its truth is failed as `stale`, because a stale acknowledgement is
indistinguishable to the next reader from a live one, and it is the row
that gets believed.
FIELDS
gate         the gate's label EXACTLY as tools/ci/_gate_dispatch.sh
records it. A label that matches nothing in the record is
failed as `stale`, so a drifting label cannot go quiet.
since        the commit at which the gate went red. The clock is commits
and not wall time so that every reader of the same tree
computes the same age with no persisted run history.
max_commits  how many commits this red may survive before this file
fails the landing gate. Required — an acknowledgement with
no bound never comes due, which is the state being removed.
owner        the issue or PR that will close it.
why          why it is red, in one sentence, for the reader who finds
this file six weeks from now.
adjudicated  present when a ruling has been written down for this row: the
verdict and where to read it. A row carrying one is NOT to be
renewed by moving `since` forward -- the ruling replaced the
question the deadline was asking.
bound_because why max_commits is THAT number and not a larger one. Not read
by the adjudicator -- read by the reviewer, who is the only
defence against a bound chosen for comfort. A bound whose
reason is 'so the board stays green' is the thing this file
exists to catch.

acknowledged.why: Went red at 487ac9844 ('a refusal that hid behind an undetermined, in both campaigns') — MEASURED by single-step bisection: rc 2 at 487ac9844^, rc 1 at 487ac9844. The gate now reaches TWO refusals over 14 published cross-layer records that an undetermined verdict had been masking. This is a gate that can finally SEE its corpus and is refusing a published comparison; the red is the finding. It closes when the two refused records are re-filed or re-measured, not when the gate is re-aimed.
acknowledged.bound_because: MEASURED cadence: 1088 commits in the last 14 days on this branch's history = ~78/day, so 200 commits is ~2.6 days. The repair is re-filing or re-measuring TWO published records — a lane edit, not a campaign re-run — which is days of work, not weeks. The bound is deliberately shorter than the 210 the L-doc row took, because nothing here waits on a place-and-route run.

acknowledged.why: Went red at 487ac9844, the same commit and the same cause as the cross-layer row — MEASURED: rc 2 at 487ac9844^, rc 1 at 487ac9844. One of the two published end-to-end records carries a refusal that had been hidden behind an undetermined. Closes when that record is re-filed or re-measured.
acknowledged.bound_because: Same bound and same measurement as the cross-layer row, because it is the same commit, the same cause and the same repair on ONE record. Giving it a longer clock than its twin would let the pair be closed one at a time and the second one forgotten.

acknowledged.why: Went red at ec43bba14 ('an rc 2 that named the artefact it READ, not the one it awaits') — MEASURED by single-step bisection: rc 2 at its parent d9a55b005, rc 1 at ec43bba14. The gate now separates two questions it used to fold together: 54 of 91 records in ppa-crosslayer/records/trials/b000/records_flat.json are REFUSED, and those findings do NOT depend on a denominator. Coverage itself stays UNDETERMINED for want of an `expected` list. THE REPAIR IS RE-PRODUCING THE RECORDS, NOT FIXING CODE, and an earlier version of this row said the opposite. MEASURED: all 54 refused records carry source.parser_sha256 sha256:054a956d923c110d53b6fd5..., while the shipped _ppa/backends/opensta.py hashes to sha256:f9dd6f34dc8850b4949d326... Both defects the refusals name are ALREADY FIXED upstream of these bytes: the 26 SAME_ARTEFACT_TWO_VALUES rows have no path_startpoint/path_endpoint/path_ordinal in scope, which _ppa/timing.py has emitted since v1.11.33 precisely so several paths in one (clock, check) view stop colliding; and the 30 scope.clock=null rows come from before timing.py grew the `p.clock is None: continue` guard it now carries. The records predate their own producer. This closes when trials/b000 is re-produced with the current backend, not when anybody edits a program.
acknowledged.bound_because: MEASURED cadence ~78 commits/day, so 200 commits is ~2.6 days. THE BOUND IS LEFT WHERE IT WAS EVEN THOUGH THE REASONING BEHIND IT WAS WRONG. It was first justified as 'code, not a re-measurement'; the repair is in fact a re-measurement, which is the more expensive job, so the honest instinct is to lengthen the clock. That instinct is exactly what 'never extend a bound' forbids, and extending it here would be an author widening his own deadline using his own corrected reasoning. 200 stands. If it expires before trials/b000 is re-produced, that is a conversation the gatekeeper should be forced to have, which is what an expiring clock is for.
